newsitem.title: ISRAEL: RESEARCH ALERT-Dead Sea Works a buy.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT-Dead Sea Works a buy.

text.p: Sahar Securities and Investments Ltd in a report released on Sunday has rated Israel's Dead Sea Works a buy but said it carries a high degree of risk.

Analyst Boaz Leviatan said Dead Sea Works is undergoing a fundamental transformation from a one-product to a multi-product company. The transition held "great potential coupled with great risk," he said.
He said weak fourth-quarter results would result in short-term weakness for the company's share price, making it a good time to buy.

"We believe that the company is managed well and is on the right track in making the transition to a larger-volume company with considerably greater profits, despite the anticipated difficulties," the report said.
Dead Sea Works, a subsidiary of Israel Chemicals Ltd, now earns most of its revenues from potash, which is used for making certain fertilisers.

The change in the company is being led by a giant ferrous magnesium joint venture with Volkswagen AG. The plant is expected to reach full capacity in the year 2000 and could make Dead Sea Works one of the largest magnesium producers in the world.
"Dead Sea Works' investment in the project is nearly equal to the company's shareholders equity and involves great risk," Leviatan said, citing questions about worldwide demand for magnesium.
Nevertheless, Leviatan forecast earnings of 0.40 shekel per share in 1996 compared with 0.39 shekel in 1995. He estimated they would reach 0.49 shekel this year and 0.60 shekel in 1998.
